sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia. Mysuru (Mysore) is a historic royal city in southern Karnataka. All records needs_review.

places.name: Mysore Palace
places.description: Among the most-visited monuments in India, the official residence of the Wadiyar dynasty. The current 1912 Indo-Saracenic building features a blend of Hindu, Muslim, Rajput and Gothic architecture with ornate interiors. The palace is illuminated by 100,000 light bulbs every Sunday and on special occasions. Budget 1.5–2 hours.

places.name: Chamundi Hills
places.description: 1062m hill overlooking Mysuru, topped by the Sri Chamundeswari Temple (12th century), dedicated to the goddess Chamundi who slew the demon Mahishasura. Accessible by road or 1000-step staircase from the city. The giant Nandi (bull) statue at the 700th step is notable. Temple crowded on weekends; earlier visits recommended.

places.name: St. Philomena's Cathedral
places.description: Neo-Gothic cathedral built 1933–1941, inspired by Cologne Cathedral in Germany. One of the largest churches in Asia with two 54m spires. Stained glass windows with biblical scenes; an underground crypt with the tomb of St. Philomena. Free entry; a major Catholic pilgrimage site.

places.name: Devaraja Market
places.description: Mysuru's century-old public market, a riot of colour with stalls selling jasmine and rose garlands, silk fabrics, spices (particularly Mysuru's famous incense), vegetables and traditional Mysuru-style bangles. The flower market section is most atmospheric at dawn. Free to browse.

places.name: Brindavan Gardens
places.description: Terraced ornamental garden at the base of the Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) dam, 16km from Mysuru. Famous for its illuminated musical fountain show in the evenings. The symmetrical gardens with fountains, topiaries and flowerbeds are best at sunset when the illumination begins. Separate entry fees for upper and lower gardens.

places.name: Srirangapatna
places.description: Historic fortified island-town in the Kaveri River 14km from Mysuru, the former capital of Tipu Sultan. Sites include the Ranganathaswamy Temple, Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace, Daria Daulat Bagh museum and the Gumbaz mausoleum. A full half-day trip from Mysuru; typically combined with Brindavan Gardens.

places.name: Mysuru Zoo
places.description: One of India's oldest and best-managed zoos, established in 1892 and covering 157 acres. Houses gorillas, tigers, giraffes, elephants and over 150 species. Well-landscaped spacious enclosures. Particularly good for families; plan 2–3 hours. Adjacent to the Mysore Palace.

places.name: Jaganmohan Palace & Art Gallery
places.description: 19th-century palace housing an extensive art collection including Raja Ravi Varma paintings, musical instruments used by Mysore royals, antiquities and natural history exhibits. One of Karnataka's best art museums; undervisited compared to the main Mysore Palace despite being adjacent. Budget 1 hour.

places.name: Nagarhole National Park
places.description: Rajiv Gandhi National Park — 640 sq km tiger and elephant reserve 95km from Mysuru, forming part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Excellent wildlife viewing: elephants, tigers, leopards, gaur, deer and 270+ bird species. Morning and evening jeep safaris; no vehicle self-entry. Accommodation inside the park at Jungle Lodges resorts.

places.name: Silk Weaving Factories
places.description: Mysuru is India's leading producer of Mysore silk, known for its pure zari (gold/silver thread) weaving. Several government-run factories (KSIC — Karnataka Silk Industries Corporation) open showrooms for visitors where handloom weavers can be observed. The Cauvery Emporium on Sayaji Rao Road is the best one-stop retail destination.
